title: Seven Days in the Saddle
statement: A cyclist rides on each of $7$ consecutive days. The mean distance ridden per day is $10$ km over the first $4$ days, $16$ km over the last $4$ days, and $12$ km over all $7$ days. How many kilometres does the cyclist ride on the fourth day?
hints: Means are awkward to combine directly. For each of the three groups of days, work out the total distance ridden.

Each group's total is its mean multiplied by its number of days. Now use inclusion-exclusion: the first four days and the last four days together cover the whole week, so ask which day belongs to both groups.

The three totals are $40$ km for the first four days, $64$ km for the last four days and $84$ km for the week. Adding the first two totals counts day $4$ twice and every other day once, so this sum exceeds the week's total by exactly the distance ridden on day $4$.
solution: Days $1$ to $4$ total $4\cdot10=40$ km, days $4$ to $7$ total $4\cdot16=64$ km, and all seven days total $7\cdot12=84$ km. Adding the first two totals counts day $4$ twice and every other day once, so the distance on day $4$ is $40+64-84=20$ km.
